tasks.acceptance_prose: Audit the statistical claims in paper/g4_academic_paper.md. Write ONLY reviews/stats-audit.md — never modify the paper or code. Steps: (1) Read paper/g4_academic_paper.md in full. (2) Run: python paper/cam_sim.py --self-check — verify it prints [OK]. (3) Run: python paper/cam_sim.py --seeds 1,2,3 --scenarios 20 --quiet to verify the code executes. (4) Internal consistency: do abstract numbers match section 8.1 tables? Do section 8.3 findings match section 8.4? Do sections 9-10 claims match section 8? Check: baseline -170.03, cam_multisignal +206.13 at 98.9% match, oracle +210.00, bid_calibrated +530.45 ROAS 26.4. (5) Statistical validity: are CIs mean +/- 1.96*SE? Are p-values plausible for the effect sizes and d-values? Are Cohen's d values consistent with the profit differences and CI widths? (6) Methodology-code match: does section 7.1 agent ladder and Appendix A match the actual agents in paper/cam_sim.py (CAMMultisignal, CAMMultisignalLearned, BidCalibratedAgent, BudgetPacedAgent)? Write reviews/stats-audit.md with sections: Summary, Internal Consistency, Statistical Validity, Methodology-Code Match, Findings (numbered), VERDICT (PASS/CONCERNS/FAIL with 1-sentence justification).

tasks.acceptance_prose: Write a structured threats-to-validity review of paper/g4_academic_paper.md using the Cook and Campbell framework. Write ONLY reviews/threats-to-validity.md — never modify the paper or code. Steps: (1) Read paper/g4_academic_paper.md in full. (2) Read paper/cam_sim.py to understand the simulation design (situation-action reward table, synthetic environment, agent implementations). (3) Analyze four threat categories: Internal Validity (are causal claims warranted? paired-seed design adequate? confounds? selection bias?); External Validity (generalization to real campaigns? ecological validity of the synthetic environment? situation-action mapping realism?); Construct Validity (do operationalizations capture the theoretical constructs? is match rate a valid proxy? is profit the right outcome?); Statistical Conclusion Validity (are tests appropriate? sample sizes adequate? multiple comparisons? effect-size interpretation?). (4) For each threat: is it addressed in the paper (check section 9.2 Limitations)? How well? What would strengthen it? (5) Write reviews/threats-to-validity.md with sections: Summary, Internal Validity, External Validity, Construct Validity, Statistical Conclusion Validity, Priority Recommendations (top 5 things a JM/Marketing Science reviewer would flag).

tasks.title: Add --bootstrap flag to paper/cam_sim.py: N bootstrap resamples of the per-seed profit data reporting BCa confidence intervals for every agent mean profit alongside existing normal-approx CIs. Gate: --self-check must still pass byte-identically. Do NOT modify the paper.
tasks.accept: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python paper/cam_sim.py --self-check 2>&1 | grep -q 'OK' && PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python paper/cam_sim.py --help 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--bootstrap' && git diff --quiet paper/g4_academic_paper.md
tasks.acceptance_prose: Add a --bootstrap flag to paper/cam_sim.py. Do NOT modify paper/g4_academic_paper.md. Requirements: (1) Add --bootstrap (int, default 0 = off; N>0 = number of resamples, e.g. 1000) to argparse. (2) When N>0, after the normal run, resample the per-seed profit data with replacement N times (50 seeds total; resample 50 with replacement), recompute each agent mean profit per resample, and report BCa confidence intervals. (3) BCa implementation: compute the bias-correction factor from the proportion of bootstrap means below the observed mean. For acceleration, use the jackknife estimate (leave-one-out influence) or set to 0 and document this simplification in a comment. (4) Output: print a stdout table (agent | mean | BCa low | BCa high | normal low | normal high) and add a bootstrap_cis dict to the JSON output if --output is set. (5) Verify: python paper/cam_sim.py --self-check still passes byte-identically (the bootstrap only activates when the flag is set). (6) Also verify: python paper/cam_sim.py --bootstrap 200 --seeds 1,2,3 --scenarios 20 --quiet runs and prints the table. Read paper/cam_sim.py carefully — the per-seed data lives in run_env results structure. Use only numpy/scipy (already imported).

tasks.title: Add --convergence flag to paper/cam_sim.py: run simulation at 10/20/30/40/50 seeds and report whether key metrics (cam_multisignal profit, Spearman rho, baseline profit) have stabilized. Gate: --self-check must still pass. Do NOT modify the paper.
tasks.accept: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python paper/cam_sim.py --self-check 2>&1 | grep -q 'OK' && PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python paper/cam_sim.py --help 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--convergence' && git diff --quiet paper/g4_academic_paper.md
tasks.acceptance_prose: Add a --convergence flag to paper/cam_sim.py. Do NOT modify paper/g4_academic_paper.md. This builds on the --bootstrap flag that must already exist in the code. Requirements: (1) Add --convergence (store_true flag) to argparse. (2) When set, run the simulation at seed counts [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] (using seeds 1..N for each run, --scenarios 200 default). For each seed count, compute: cam_multisignal mean profit, Spearman rho between context match rate and profit across agents, and baseline mean profit. (3) A metric is STABLE when the mean over the last 10 seeds differs from the overall mean by less than 5%. Report: seeds N | cam_multisignal profit | rho | baseline profit | stable (YES/NO per metric). (4) Print a stdout table and add a convergence dict to the JSON output if --output is set. (5) Verify: python paper/cam_sim.py --self-check still passes byte-identically. (6) Also verify: python paper/cam_sim.py --convergence --seeds 1,2,3,4,5 --scenarios 20 runs and prints the table. Read paper/cam_sim.py carefully. Use scipy.stats.spearmanr for rho.
